## Big Picture Overview

### What Problem Does This App Solve?

**Problem:**
Clinical geneticists have identified 153 SYNGAP1 gene variants across patient populations, but:
- Variant data is scattered across spreadsheets
- Hard to visualize variant locations on the gene
- No easy way to find variants with research resources (biosamples, cell lines, mouse models)
- cDNA notation is relative to transcript, but visualization requires genome coordinates

**Solution:**
An interactive web app that:
1. Displays all variants on an actual genome browser (IGV)
2. Groups variants by type (missense, nonsense, frameshift, etc.)
3. Filters by available research resources
4. Automatically converts cDNA coordinates to genome positions
5. Runs in any web browser (no installation for end users)

---

## Design Philosophy

### Core Principles That Guided Development

#### 1. **Separation of Concerns**
```
DATA LAYER       → Load, parse, transform, cache
BUSINESS LOGIC   → Filter, format, compute
PRESENTATION     → Display, interact, visualize
```

**Why:** Each layer can be modified independently. Data changes don't break UI. UI redesign doesn't affect data processing.

#### 2. **Performance Through Preprocessing**
```
Do expensive work ONCE at startup
   ↓
   Parse variants
   Query API
   Cache results
   Format data
   ↓
User interactions are INSTANT
```

**Why:** Users don't wait for data processing during interactions. App feels responsive.

#### 3. **Reactive Programming**
```
User changes filter
   ↓ (automatic)
Data re-filtered
   ↓ (automatic)
UI updates
   ↓ (automatic)
Tracks refresh
```

**Why:** No manual update logic. No bugs from forgetting to update something. Declarative code.

#### 4. **Fail Gracefully**
```
Variant has no coordinate? → Skip it, continue
API call fails? → Return NA, don't crash
Filter removes all data? → Show empty track, explain
```

**Why:** Real-world data is messy. App should handle edge cases without breaking.

#### 5. **Cache Everything Expensive**
```
Ensembl exon structure → Pre-built by svv_build_cache.R; loaded from disk (6-month expiry)
ClinVar API calls      → Pre-built by svv_build_cache.R; loaded from disk (7-day expiry)
Parsed data            → Computed once (session)
Filtered data          → Reactive (auto-cached)
```

**Why:** Decoupling cache-building from app startup means the app launches in < 5 seconds regardless of network conditions. Single-call exon fetch + local arithmetic (in the cache builder) eliminates 143 per-coordinate API calls. Works fully offline between cache refreshes. Reduces external API load.

## Data Flow Diagram

### Startup Sequence
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ APP STARTUP (Happens Once)                                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

1. Load Libraries
   ├─ shiny, igvShiny, dplyr, stringr, httr, jsonlite, shinyWidgets, readxl
   └─ Why: Each provides specific functionality

1B. Load ClinVar Data (from pre-built cache)
   ├─ Read cache/clinvar/clinvar_data.rds from disk (< 1 ms)
   ├─ If cache absent → warn and continue with empty data frame
   └─ Cache is populated separately by svv_build_cache.R

2. Load 2024 Citizen variant data (2024_citizen_variants.csv)
   ├─ 153 variants × 33 columns; one row per unique variant
   └─ stringsAsFactors = FALSE for flexibility

3. Aggregate 2026 Citizen patient counts (2026_citizen_variants.xlsx)
   ├─ Per-patient rows → table() → named integer vector (variant → count)
   └─ Wrapped in tryCatch; missing file → 0 for all variants

4. Aggregate CureSyngap1 patient counts (curesyngap1_variants.csv)
   ├─ Per-patient rows → table() → named integer vector (variant → count)
   └─ Wrapped in tryCatch; missing file → 0 for all variants

5. Clean Variant Types
   ├─ "missense VUS" → "missense-VUS"
   ├─ "frameshift deletion" → "frameshift"
   └─ Ensures consistent naming

6. Extract cDNA Coordinates + Derive Count Columns
   ├─ "c.333del" → 333
   ├─ "c.190_200del" → 190
   ├─ citizen_2026_count: lookup variant in 2026 counts table (0 if absent)
   ├─ curesyngap1_count: lookup variant in CureSyngap1 counts table (0 if absent)
   └─ Uses regex parsing + named table lookup

7. Convert Coordinates to Genome Positions
   ├─ Read transcript exon structure from cache/transcript_structure/ (< 1 ms)
   ├─ If cache absent → warn; all positions will be NA
   ├─ Compute all cDNA→genome mappings locally via arithmetic (~1 ms)
   ├─ cDNA 333 → chr6:33,425,796
   └─ No API calls at app launch (cache populated by svv_build_cache.R)

8. Format Protein Changes
   ├─ "p.R135X" → "Arg135ter"
   └─ Three-letter codes more readable

9. Merge Everything
   ├─ Original data + coordinates + formatted names + source counts
   └─ Complete dataset ready for visualization

10. Start Web Server
   ├─ Initialize UI
   ├─ Initialize IGV browser
   └─ Wait for user interaction

svv_build_cache.R (run once before first launch): ~35–65 seconds (ClinVar fetch ~30–60 sec + exon structure fetch ~500 ms)
Every app launch: < 5 seconds (reads both caches from disk; no API calls)
```

### User Interaction Sequence
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ USER INTERACTION (Reactive)                                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Scenario 1: User clicks "missense" button
────────────────────────────────────────
1. observeEvent fires
2. Update added_tracks state (missense = TRUE)
3. Get filtered_data() (respects any active filters)
4. Filter for variant.type == "missense"
5. Convert to GFF3 format
6. Load track into IGV
7. Center view on SYNGAP1 gene
8. Track appears on screen
9. If ClinVar track is active: repin_clinvar_to_bottom() removes and
   re-adds the ClinVar track so it remains below all variant tracks

Scenario 2: User clicks "ClinVar" button
─────────────────────────────────────────
1. observeEvent fires
2. Set clinvar_track_added(TRUE)
3. Read current slider value (input$clinvar_size_kb), default 100 KB
4. Call create_clinvar_gff3_data(clinvar_data, max_size_kb = 100)
   ├─ Filter out variants with no GRCh38 coordinates
   ├─ Filter out variants whose span > 100 KB
   └─ Format remaining variants as GFF3
5. Load teal ClinVar track into IGV
   └─ Because this is a fresh load (not triggered by a variant-type button),
      ClinVar lands at the bottom of the current stack naturally
6. Center view on SYNGAP1 gene
7. Track appears on screen — pinned at the bottom

Scenario 3: User moves ClinVar size slider to 10 KB
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. observeEvent(input$clinvar_size_kb) fires
2. Check clinvar_track_added() — TRUE, so continue
3. Re-call create_clinvar_gff3_data(clinvar_data, max_size_kb = 10)
   └─ Fewer variants pass the span filter
4. Reload ClinVar track (replaces existing track, no flicker)
5. Track updates instantly to show only variants ≤ 10 KB

Scenario 4: User checks "Has biorepository samples"
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. Checkbox input changes
2. filtered_data() reactive recalculates
   ├─ Start with all variants
   ├─ Filter: biorepository column has data
   └─ Return subset
3. trackButtons UI regenerates (different variant types available)
4. observeEvent for filtered_data() fires
5. All visible internal tracks reload with filtered data
6. IGV updates (some variants disappear)
7. ClinVar track is unaffected by the filter (independent pipeline)
8. Second observeEvent for filtered_data() fires: if ClinVar is active,
   repin_clinvar_to_bottom() ensures it stays at the bottom after reloads

Scenario 5: User checks "Cell line available" too
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. Second checkbox changes
2. filtered_data() reactive recalculates again
   ├─ Start with all variants
   ├─ Filter: biorepository column has data (AND)
   ├─ Filter: iPSC.line column has data (AND)
   └─ Return smaller subset (intersection)
3. Tracks reload with even fewer variants
4. UI shows only variants with BOTH resources
```

## Component Breakdown

### Layer 1: Data Processing

**Purpose:** Transform raw CSV into visualization-ready format; fetch and cache external reference data

**Components:**

1. **ClinVar Loader** (simple `readRDS` in `svv_app.R`)
   - Input: `cache/clinvar/clinvar_data.rds` (pre-built by `svv_build_cache.R`)
   - Output: `clinvar_data` data frame (~1,900 variants with GRCh38 coordinates)
   - Cache builder: `fetch_clinvar_ids`, `fetch_clinvar_summaries`, `load_clinvar_data` in `svv_build_cache.R`
   - Expiry: 7 days — re-run `svv_build_cache.R` to refresh

2. **Amino Acid Converter** (`swap_one_letter_to_three_letter`)
   - Input: `"R135X"`
   - Output: `"Arg135ter"`
   - Why: Readability for biologists

3. **Coordinate Extractor** (`extract_cDNA_coordinate`)
   - Input: `"c.333del"`
   - Output: `333`
   - Why: Need numeric value for local coordinate mapping

4. **Transcript Exon Loader** (simple `readRDS` in `svv_app.R`)
   - Input: `cache/transcript_structure/ENST00000418600.rds` (pre-built by `svv_build_cache.R`)
   - Output: Data frame of exons sorted in transcript order (strand-aware)
   - Cache builder: `fetch_transcript_exons` in `svv_build_cache.R` (single Ensembl API call replacing 143+ per-coordinate calls)
   - Expiry: 6 months — re-run `svv_build_cache.R` to refresh

5. **Local Coordinate Mapper** (`build_cdna_position_map`)
   - Input: Vector of cDNA coordinates + exon data frame
   - Output: Data frame with genome positions (seqid, start, end)
   - Pure arithmetic — no network calls
   - Why: cDNA→exon arithmetic is deterministic and matches Ensembl's own mapping exactly

6. **Data Loader**
   - Reads `2024_citizen_variants.csv` (153 variants; pre-aggregated patient counts)
   - Aggregates per-variant counts from `2026_citizen_variants.xlsx` via `table()`
   - Aggregates per-variant counts from `curesyngap1_variants.csv` via `table()`
   - Normalizes variant types
   - Extracts cDNA coordinates
   - Joins source counts as `citizen_2026_count` and `curesyngap1_count` columns
   - Maps to genome positions (locally)
   - Merges results into complete dataset

### Layer 2: User Interface

**Purpose:** Visual layout and controls

**Components:**

1. **Title Bar**
   - Shows app name
   - Professional appearance

2. **Sidebar Panel**
   - Dynamic variant type buttons (generated by server)
   - Three research asset filter checkboxes (above the ClinVar divider)
   - Static ClinVar track button (below a divider)
   - Log-spaced size filter slider for ClinVar (1–50,000 KB, default 100 KB)
   - Compact width (30% of screen)

3. **Main Panel**
   - IGV browser widget
   - Large display area (70% of screen)
   - 700px height for multiple tracks

4. **Footer**
   - Citation for igvShiny tool
   - Centered, small font

**Layout Choice:**
```
┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         SYNGAP1 Variant Viewer         │
├──────────────┬─────────────────────────┤
│              │                         │
│  [missense]  │                         │
│  [nonsense]  │      IGV Browser        │
│  [frameshift]│      (Genome View)      │
│  ...         │                         │
│  □ Biorepository                       │
│  □ Cell line │                         │
│  □ Mouse line│                         │
│ ──────────── │                         │
│  [ClinVar]   │                         │
│  |~~~size~~| │                         │
│              │                         │
└──────────────┴─────────────────────────┘
  30% width         70% width
```

### Layer 3: Server Logic

**Purpose:** Reactive programming that connects UI to data

**Components:**

1. **Internal Track State Manager** (`added_tracks`)
   - Tracks which variant-type buttons user has clicked
   - Persists across filter changes
   - Type: `reactiveVal(list())`

2. **ClinVar Track State Manager** (`clinvar_track_added`)
   - Separate flag for whether the ClinVar track is currently displayed
   - Prevents the size slider observer from firing before the track exists
   - Type: `reactiveVal(FALSE)`

3. **Data Filter** (`filtered_data`)
   - Reactive expression
   - Recomputes when any filter checkbox changes
   - Returns: Subset of variant_data matching all active filters
   - Note: Does not affect ClinVar data (independent reference dataset)

4. **Button Generator** (`output$trackButtons`)
   - Reactive UI
   - Creates buttons based on filtered variant types
   - Updates when filters change

5. **Internal Track Loader** (`observe` with button events)
   - Listens for variant-type button clicks
   - Converts data to GFF3 format
   - Loads track into IGV
   - Handles empty data gracefully

6. **ClinVar Track Loader** (`observeEvent(input$addTrack_clinvar)`)
   - Listens for ClinVar button click
   - Sets `clinvar_track_added(TRUE)`
   - Calls `create_clinvar_gff3_data()` with current slider value
   - Loads teal ClinVar track into IGV

7. **ClinVar Size Slider Handler** (`observeEvent(input$clinvar_size_kb)`)
   - Fires when user moves the size filter slider
   - No-op if `clinvar_track_added()` is FALSE (track not yet displayed)
   - Re-builds GFF3 with new KB threshold and reloads track live

8. **Track Updater** (`observeEvent(filtered_data())`)
   - Watches for filter changes
   - Reloads all visible internal tracks with new filtered data
   - Keeps display in sync with filters

9. **IGV Initializer** (`output$igvShiny_0`)
   - Sets up genome browser on startup
   - Configures genome (hg38)
   - Sets initial view (SYNGAP1)
   - Starts with no tracks

## Key Design Decisions

### Decision 1: When to Process Data?

**Options:**
- A) Process data when user requests it (lazy loading)
- B) Process all data at startup (eager loading)

**Chosen: B (Eager Loading)**

**Rationale:**
- Dataset is small (153 variants)
- Startup delay acceptable (~1 second with cache)
- User interactions must be instant
- Simpler code (no loading states)
- Better UX (no waiting during use)

**Trade-off:** Longer startup vs instant interactions → Choose instant interactions

---

### Decision 2: How to Handle cDNA→Genome Coordinate Conversion?

**Options:**
- A) Query Ensembl `/map/cdna/` endpoint once per variant coordinate at startup (memoized)
- B) Fetch the complete transcript exon structure once; compute all mappings locally

**Chosen: B (Single exon-structure fetch + local arithmetic)**

**Rationale:**
- One API call replaces 143+ per-coordinate calls
- Local arithmetic is deterministic and matches Ensembl's own mapping exactly
- Cold-cache startup drops from ~8–12 minutes to under 30 seconds
- Adding new variants to the CSV costs nothing at startup — exon table already cached
- Exon structure for a stable transcript like ENST00000418600 changes rarely; 6-month cache is more than conservative

**Trade-off:** Manual cache invalidation if Ensembl updates the annotation → mitigated by a 6-month time-based expiry that handles this automatically

---

### Decision 3: What Happens When Filters Remove All Data?

**Options:**
- A) Hide the track completely
- B) Show empty track with message
- C) Disable the button

**Chosen: B (Show Empty Track)**

**Rationale:**
- User feedback (track exists, just filtered out)
- Consistent behavior (all clicks do something)
- Less confusing than disappearing tracks
- Easy to understand why track is empty

**Trade-off:** Visual clutter vs clarity → Choose clarity

---

### Decision 4: How to Structure Filter Logic?

**Options:**
- A) OR logic (any filter matches)
- B) AND logic (all filters match)
- C) Complex boolean logic

**Chosen: B (AND Logic)**

**Rationale:**
- "Show variants with biorepository AND cell line"
- Natural interpretation
- Most useful for research planning
- Simple to implement
- Easy to explain to users

**Trade-off:** Flexibility vs simplicity → Choose simplicity

---

### Decision 5: Where to Store Genome Positions?

**Options:**
- A) In CSV file
- B) Query API each time
- C) Cache in memory
- D) Cache on disk permanently

**Chosen: D (Disk Cache) with path to migrate to A**

**Current Approach:**
```
CSV → Extract coords → Check cache → (API if needed) → Display
```

**Better Future Approach:**
```
Enhanced CSV (with positions) → Display
```

**Rationale:**
- Current: Good enough, works now
- Future: Simpler, faster, more reliable
- Migration path: Extract cache → CSV → Remove API code

## Development Timeline (How the App Was Built)

### Phase 1: Prototype (The "desktop" File)
```
Goal: Prove concept
Approach: Hardcode everything
Result: 160 hardcoded positions, single track
Learning: IGV integration works!
```

**Code:**
```r
startPathogenic <- c(33420307, 33420332, ...)  # 160 positions
loadBedTrack(..., tbl=tbl.pathogenic, color="red")
```

**Limitations:**
- Can't add new variants without editing code
- No filtering
- No variant type distinction
- Not maintainable

### Phase 2: Data-Driven Design
```
Goal: Load from CSV
Approach: Read 2024_citizen_variants.csv
Result: Dynamic variant loading
Learning: Need coordinate conversion!
```

**Challenge:** CSV has cDNA coordinates, IGV needs genome coordinates

**Solution:** Ensembl REST API

### Phase 3: API Integration
```
Goal: Convert coordinates automatically
Approach: Query Ensembl API
Result: Working but slow (40 seconds startup)
Learning: Need caching!
```

**Problem:**
```
143 variants × 300ms per API call = 42,900ms = 43 seconds
```

**Unacceptable for production app**

### Phase 4: Performance Optimization
```
Goal: Fast cold-cache startup (was 8–12 minutes)
Approach: Fetch transcript exon structure once; compute all mappings locally
Result: Cold-cache startup under 30 seconds; subsequent runs under 5 seconds
Learning: Restructuring the problem (one fetch + arithmetic) beats caching many calls!
```

**The problem with per-coordinate memoization:**
```
143 variants × 300ms per API call = 42,900ms = ~43 seconds on cold cache
Cache only helps after first build — if cache is absent or corrupted, full delay returns
```

**The new approach:**
```r
# Fetch the exon structure once
transcript_exons <- fetch_transcript_exons("ENST00000418600")  # ~500 ms, 1 call

# Map all coordinates locally with arithmetic — no further API calls
positions_df <- build_cdna_position_map(
  coords  = variant_data$cDNA_coordinate,
  exon_df = transcript_exons
)  # ~1 ms
```

**Performance:**
```
Before: 8–12 minutes (cold cache), ~2 seconds (warm cache)
After:  ~30 seconds total (cold), <5 seconds (warm)
Key insight: The exon table is the only data needed; per-coordinate API calls were redundant
```

### Phase 5: Rich UI Features
```
Goal: Multiple variant types, filtering
Approach: Dynamic buttons, reactive filters
Result: Professional research tool
Learning: Reactive programming is powerful!
```

**Added:**
- Color-coded variant types
- Dynamic button generation
- Research asset filters
- Graceful empty state handling
- Track updates on filter changes

### Phase 6: Polish & Documentation
```
Goal: Production-ready code
Approach: Comments, error handling, citation
Result: Maintainable, documented application
Learning: Documentation is essential!
```

### Phase 7: ClinVar Integration & Size Filter
```
Goal: Add live ClinVar reference data alongside internal variants
Approach: NCBI E-utilities API with time-limited cache
Result: Toggleable ClinVar track with log-spaced size filter slider
Learning: Two caches with different lifetimes need different strategies!
```

**Added:**
- ClinVar fetch via NCBI esearch + esummary (batched, rate-limited) — in `svv_build_cache.R`
- 7-day time-limited cache (`cache/clinvar/`) with stale-cache fallback — managed by `svv_build_cache.R`
- `create_clinvar_gff3_data()` with `max_size_kb` parameter — in `svv_app.R`
- Static ClinVar button (separate from dynamic variant-type loop)
- `clinvar_track_added` state flag to gate the slider observer
- `shinyWidgets::sliderTextInput()` with log-spaced stops (1–50,000 KB)
- Live track reload on slider change

### Phase 8: Cold-Cache Startup Optimization
```
Goal: Eliminate 8–12 minute cold-cache delay
Problem: Per-coordinate Ensembl API calls via memoise were O(N) at startup
Approach: Fetch transcript exon structure once; compute all mappings locally
Result: Cold-cache startup under 30 seconds; warm-cache startup unchanged
```

**Root cause:**
```
143 unique cDNA coordinates × ~300ms per /map/cdna/ call = ~43 seconds (Ensembl only)
memoise permanent cache helped warm starts, but cold-cache was still O(N) API calls
```

**Architectural change:**
- Replaced `get_genome_positions_function` + `memoise` + `cachem::cache_disk` with:
  - `fetch_transcript_exons()` — one call, returns full exon table
  - `build_cdna_position_map()` — pure arithmetic, no network
  - `transcript_cache_is_fresh()` / `write_transcript_cache()` — 6-month time-based expiry
- Removed `memoise` and `cachem` package dependencies
- Old approach preserved on the `slow-cache-option` branch

### Phase 9: UI Polish & ClinVar Track Pinning
```
Goal: Improve sidebar clarity and ClinVar track positioning
Changes: Three targeted UI fixes — no data pipeline or API changes
```

**Changes made:**

- **Sidebar reorder**: Research asset filter checkboxes (biorepository, cell line, mouse line)
  moved above the horizontal `hr()` separator so all internal-data controls are visually
  grouped together. The ClinVar button and size slider remain below the separator as the
  clearly distinct external-reference section.

- **Track label rename**: The `missense-VUS` button now displays as **"VUS (missense only)"**.
  The internal variant type identifier (`missense-VUS`) used throughout the data pipeline,
  GFF3 formatting, color table, and `observeEvent` observers is unchanged — only the
  `actionButton` label rendered in the sidebar is affected, via a `track_label_map` lookup
  in `output$trackButtons`. A factor-to-character coercion (`as.character(type)`) is applied
  before the lookup to avoid `[[` treating factor levels as integer indices.

- **ClinVar bottom-pinning**: Added `repin_clinvar_to_bottom()` helper (Section 9C) that
  calls `removeTracksByName()` followed by `loadGFF3TrackFromLocalData()` for the ClinVar
  track, forcing IGV to re-append it at the bottom of the stack. Called in two places:
  1. Inside the variant-type button `observeEvent`, after each new track load.
  2. In a dedicated `observeEvent(filtered_data())` observer, after filter-driven track
     reloads complete.

### Phase 10: Feature Popup Size Field
```
Goal: Surface genomic span directly in the variant click popup
Changes: GFF3 attributes extended in create_gff3_data() and create_clinvar_gff3_data()
```

**Changes made:**

- **`create_gff3_data()` (Section 9)**: Added `Size` as the final attribute in both branches
  of the `ifelse` that builds the attributes string. Computed as `end - start` from the GFF3
  columns already present in the `mutate` block — no new data sources required. Displayed as
  bp for variants < 1,000 bp, or kb (rounded to 2 decimal places) for variants ≥ 1,000 bp.

- **`create_clinvar_gff3_data()` (Section 9B)**: Added `Size` as the final attribute after
  `OncogenicityReviewStatus`. ClinVar spans a far wider range than internal variants (SNVs
  through multi-megabase CNVs), so a three-tier display is used: Mb (≥ 1,000,000 bp), kb
  (≥ 1,000 bp), or bp. The `clean_attr()` sanitizer is intentionally skipped here since the
  value is computed arithmetic, not a raw ClinVar string that could contain GFF3 reserved
  characters (`;` or `=`).

**Why not in a separate column?**
  GFF3 carries all display metadata in the attributes string; IGV reads key=value pairs from
  that field to populate the feature detail popup. Adding a dedicated column would break the
  GFF3 format expected by `loadGFF3TrackFromLocalData()`.

### Phase 11: Cache-Builder Separation
```
Goal: Decouple external API calls from Shiny app startup
Changes: Cache-building code moved from svv_app.R into standalone svv_build_cache.R
```

**Changes made:**

- `svv_build_cache.R` is now the **canonical** home for all cache-building logic: ClinVar
  E-utilities fetch functions (`fetch_clinvar_ids`, `fetch_clinvar_summaries`,
  `load_clinvar_data`) and the Ensembl transcript fetch (`fetch_transcript_exons`,
  `write_transcript_cache`, `transcript_cache_is_fresh`).

- `svv_app.R` now contains only two simple `readRDS` stubs — one for `clinvar_data` and
  one for `transcript_exons` — with graceful empty-frame / NULL fallbacks if the cache
  files are absent.

- `library(httr)` and `library(jsonlite)` removed from `svv_app.R` (no longer needed;
  retained in `svv_build_cache.R` which still makes HTTP requests).

**Why:**
  Running the app no longer requires outbound network access at launch time. The Shiny
  process simply reads from disk, making startup faster and more predictable in restricted
  network environments. `svv_build_cache.R` can be run on a schedule (cron, GitHub Actions)
  or manually to keep the caches fresh.

### Phase 12: Single-Base Variant Size Fix
```
Goal: Correct "0 bp" Size display for point variants in the feature popup
Change: Floor the size calculation to 1 bp in create_gff3_data() and
        create_clinvar_gff3_data()
```

**Root cause:**

Both `create_gff3_data()` and `create_clinvar_gff3_data()` compute genomic span as
`end - start` (or `clinvar_end - clinvar_start`). For single-base variants (SNVs,
single-base deletions, frameshifts, etc.) the `start` and `end` coordinates are
identical, so the subtraction evaluates to `0`, producing "0 bp" in the popup.

For ClinVar specifically, this was a latent consequence of the v3.0.1 fix: removing the
`+1` end-coordinate offset from `parse_esummary_record` was correct for IGV rendering,
but it meant that SNVs — which arrive from NCBI with `start == stop` — now also produce
`clinvar_end - clinvar_start == 0` in the size field.

**Fix:**

Replaced all raw difference expressions with `pmax(..., 1L)` — R's vectorized
element-wise maximum — so each row's size floors at 1 bp without affecting multi-base
variants whose span is already ≥ 1.

*Internal variants (`create_gff3_data()`)* — applied to both branches of the
`attributes` `ifelse` (no-protein-change and has-protein-change):

```r
# Before
";Size=", ifelse(
  (end - start) >= 1000,
  paste0(round((end - start) / 1000, 2), " kb"),
  paste0(end - start, " bp")
)

# After
";Size=", ifelse(
  pmax(end - start, 1L) >= 1000,
  paste0(round(pmax(end - start, 1L) / 1000, 2), " kb"),
  paste0(pmax(end - start, 1L), " bp")
)
```

*ClinVar variants (`create_clinvar_gff3_data()`)* — applied across all three tiers of
the nested `ifelse` (Mb / kb / bp):

```r
# Before
";Size=", ifelse(
  (clinvar_end - clinvar_start) >= 1e6,
  paste0(round((clinvar_end - clinvar_start) / 1e6, 2), " Mb"),
  ifelse(
    (clinvar_end - clinvar_start) >= 1000,
    paste0(round((clinvar_end - clinvar_start) / 1000, 2), " kb"),
    paste0(clinvar_end - clinvar_start, " bp")
  )
)

# After
";Size=", ifelse(
  pmax(clinvar_end - clinvar_start, 1L) >= 1e6,
  paste0(round(pmax(clinvar_end - clinvar_start, 1L) / 1e6, 2), " Mb"),
  ifelse(
    pmax(clinvar_end - clinvar_start, 1L) >= 1000,
    paste0(round(pmax(clinvar_end - clinvar_start, 1L) / 1000, 2), " kb"),
    paste0(pmax(clinvar_end - clinvar_start, 1L), " bp")
  )
)
```

**No changes to:** UI, filters, data pipeline, or caches. No cache invalidation required.

### Phase 13: Multi-Source Patient Count Display & File Renaming
```
Goal: Show per-database patient counts in the variant popup
Problem: Single "Number of patients" field gave no source context
Approach: Load two additional per-patient-row files; aggregate counts at startup
Result: Variant popup now shows 2024 Citizen Count, 2026 Citizen Count,
        and CureSyngap1 Survey Count as three separate fields
```

**New data sources:**

| File | Format | Count derivation |
|---|---|---|
| `2024_citizen_variants.csv` | One row per unique variant | Pre-aggregated in `X..patients.in.Citizen.Health` column |
| `2026_citizen_variants.xlsx` | One row per patient | `table(raw$variant)` at startup |
| `curesyngap1_variants.csv` | One row per patient | `table(raw$variant)` at startup |

**Key implementation decisions:**

- Files kept **separate** rather than merged into one CSV — preserves data provenance, allows each source to be updated independently, and avoids the awkward "mixed-grain" problem (the 2024 file is pre-aggregated; the other two are per-patient)
- Both new loaders wrapped in `tryCatch` — a missing file produces `0` counts for that source instead of crashing the app
- Count columns added to `variant_data` during the existing `mutate()` preprocessing block so they are available everywhere downstream without restructuring any other code
- `create_gff3_data()` attributes string updated in both branches (`ifelse`) — no change to the GFF3 column structure, only the content of the attributes field
- Added `library(readxl)` for `.xlsx` reading; `svv_packages.R` updated to install and verify it

**Files renamed for clarity:**
- `updatedCitizen191.csv` → `2024_citizen_variants.csv`
- `curesyngap1_variants_clean.csv` → `curesyngap1_variants.csv`

No changes to coordinate mapping, ClinVar integration, filters, UI layout, or caches.

### Pattern 1: Single-Fetch + Local Arithmetic for Coordinate Mapping
```r
# Fetch the data structure once (1 API call)
transcript_exons <- fetch_transcript_exons("ENST00000418600")

# Compute all derived values locally — no further network calls
positions_df <- build_cdna_position_map(
  coords  = variant_data$cDNA_coordinate,
  exon_df = transcript_exons
)
```

**Why this beats per-call caching:**
- Cold cache: 1 API call (~500 ms) instead of 143 calls (~43 seconds)
- Adding variants to the CSV costs nothing — exon table already covers the whole transcript
- The arithmetic is deterministic; results are identical to per-coordinate API queries
- Cache stores one compact file (the exon table) instead of hundreds of individual hash files

**When to use:** Any situation where you need to compute many derived values from a single stable data structure

---

### Pattern 2: Reactive Expression for Derived Data
```r
# Reactive expression (automatically updates)
filtered_data <- reactive({
  data <- original_data
  if (input$checkbox) {
    data <- data %>% filter(...)
  }
  data
})

# Use in outputs/observers
output$plot <- renderPlot({
  plot(filtered_data())  # Auto-updates when checkbox changes
})
```

**When to use:** Data that depends on user inputs and is used in multiple places

---

### Pattern 3: Closure to Avoid Variable Capture
```r
# WRONG - all observers share same 'type'
for (type in types) {
  observeEvent(input[[type]], {
    print(type)  # Always prints last type!
  })
}

# RIGHT - each observer gets own 't'
for (type in types) {
  local({
    t <- type  # Capture in local scope
    observeEvent(input[[t]], {
      print(t)  # Prints correct type
    })
  })
}
```

**When to use:** Observers in loops

---

### Pattern 4: Graceful Degradation
```r
result <- tryCatch({
  expensive_operation()
}, error = function(e) {
  # Return sensible default instead of crashing
  return(list(seqid = "chr6", start = NA, end = NA))
})
```

**When to use:** External dependencies, network calls, user data

---

### Pattern 5: Separate Validation from Processing
```r
# Validation wrapper
extract_protein_change <- function(protein_change) {
  if (is.na(protein_change) || protein_change == "") {
    return(protein_change)  # Handle bad input
  }
  swap_one_letter_to_three_letter(protein_change)  # Do work
}

# Processing function (assumes valid input)
swap_one_letter_to_three_letter <- function(protein_change_str) {
  # No validation needed - wrapper handles it
  # Pure transformation logic
}
```

**When to use:** Complex data transformations with edge cases

## Summary: The Full Picture

```
                    SYNGAP1 Variant Viewer
                           ↓
        ┌──────────────────┴──────────────────┐
        │                                     │
    DATA LAYER                           UI LAYER
        │                                     │
   Load CSV ────────────────────────→  Display Controls
   Parse Variants                       Show IGV Browser
   Query Ensembl (cached!) ←────────  User Clicks Button
   Fetch ClinVar (7-day cache!)         User Checks Filter
   Format Data              ←────────  User Moves Slider
        │                                     │
        └──────────────────┬──────────────────┘
                           ↓
                    REACTIVE LAYER
                   (Shiny Server)
                           │
        ┌──────────────────┼──────────────────┐
        │                  │                  │
   Filter Data      Generate UI        Load Tracks
   (reactive())   (renderUI())    (observeEvent())
        │                  │                  │
        │                  │       ┌──────────┴──────────┐
        │                  │  Internal tracks       ClinVar track
        │                  │  (filtered by          (filtered by
        │                  │   checkboxes)           size slider)
        └──────────────────┴──────────────────┘
                           ↓
                    User sees updated view
                    (tracks, filters, data)
```

**Key Insight:** 
The app maintains two parallel data pipelines. Both rely on pre-built disk caches (populated by `svv_build_cache.R`): internal variant data flows from three CSV/Excel sources → cached exon structure (readRDS) → local cDNA arithmetic → reactive filter → GFF3 → IGV, while ClinVar data flows from cached clinvar_data.rds (readRDS) → size filter → GFF3 → IGV. Both pipelines share the same IGV browser but are controlled independently — internal tracks respond to research-asset checkboxes, while the ClinVar track responds only to its own button and size slider. Neither pipeline makes outbound API calls at app launch.

**Success Criteria:**
✅ Fast (< 1 second load time after first run)
✅ Reliable (handles missing data gracefully)
✅ Useful (filters help researchers find variants)
✅ Maintainable (well-documented, modular code)
✅ Scalable (can handle more variants/filters)
